summary: Describes how to use Transport Layer Security over the Stream Control Transmission Protocol. It lets users of TLS benefit from SCTP features such as multiple streams, which avoid head-of-line blocking, and multi-homing for network-level fault tolerance, and discusses extensions needed to make it work well.

eli5.summary: SCTP can carry many conversations at once over one connection. This note shows how to keep all of them secret and tamper-proof using TLS.

questions: how does tls work over sctp
can tls use multiple sctp streams
what ciphersuite must tls over sctp support
does tls over sctp allow unordered delivery
subtitle: How to run TLS on top of SCTP, one TLS connection per bi-directional stream.

tldr.problem: TLS was designed for a reliable in-order byte stream such as TCP, while SCTP is message oriented and offers multiple streams and multi-homing.
tldr.mechanism: Each bi-directional SCTP stream carries its own TLS connection with its own handshake, and each TLS record is sent as one SCTP user message. Neither TLS nor SCTP needs changing.
tldr.outcome: TLS users get SCTP's multiple streams and multi-homing. The RFC has been updated by RFC 8996.

facts.label: Unordered delivery
facts.value: MUST NOT be used with TLS

today: RFC 3436 is a Proposed Standard that has been updated by RFC 8996. It is not obsoleted.

sections.title: Why TLS Over SCTP
sections.content:
TLS is designed to run on a byte-stream transport that delivers reliably and in sequence, and is mainly used over TCP. SCTP is message oriented and adds features TCP lacks. RFC 3436 shows how to use TLS over SCTP so the TLS user can benefit from them.

The abstract names two benefits: multiple streams, which avoid head of line blocking, and multi-homing, which gives network-level fault tolerance. The document defines how to use the multiple streams feature and how to handle the message-oriented nature of SCTP.

The method requires no changes to TLS or SCTP. The only requirement is that SCTP implementations support the optional feature of fragmenting SCTP user messages. Dynamic reconfiguration of IP addresses, then under discussion for SCTP, can also be used with this solution.
sections.eli5: TLS keeps a chat private. SCTP is a delivery service with extra features. This RFC explains how to use them together without changing either.

sections.title: What SCTP and TLS Must Provide
sections.content:
SCTP MUST provide fragmentation of user messages, an optional feature of RFC 2960, so TLS does not need to know the MTU. Because SCTP is message oriented, it must carry every TLS record as one SCTP user message. The supported maximum user message length MUST therefore be at least 2^14 + 2048 + 5 = 18437 bytes, the maximum length of a TLSCiphertext. An SCTP implementation might need the partial delivery API to support messages of this size. SCTP then fragments and reassembles the records to avoid IP fragmentation.

On the TLS side, an implementation for TLS over SCTP MUST support at least the ciphersuite TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA from RFC 3268.
sections.eli5: SCTP has to be able to carry each TLS packet whole, even a big one, by cutting it up and putting it back together itself. Everyone must also know at least one common secret code.

sections.title: Streams and Connections
sections.content:
An association between endpoints A and Z has n streams from A to Z and m streams from Z to A. Two streams with the same stream identifier are used as one bi-directional stream. An association is therefore a set of min(n,m) bi-directional streams plus (max(n,m) - min(n,m)) uni-directional streams.

TLS makes a connection over a bi-directional stream, so the number of TLS connections in an association is limited by the number of bi-directional streams. The TLS handshake runs separately on each one, and each handshake can be a full handshake or an abbreviated handshake that resumes a TLS session using a session id from another connection, on the same or another association. Handshakes are independent and can be delayed until the stream is first used for user data.
sections.eli5: A road with lanes in both directions: matching lanes pair up, and each pair gets its own private tunnel with its own start-up check.

sections.title: Using Streams for Data
sections.content:
A bi-directional stream not used for TLS carries SCTP-based user data with no restrictions. Normally a stream used for TLS SHOULD NOT also carry SCTP-based data. The exception is protocols with upgrade-to-TLS mechanisms, such as HTTP upgrade (RFC 2817) and SMTP over TLS (RFC 3207).

TLS needs records delivered in strict sequence. So the SCTP unordered delivery feature MUST NOT be used on streams carrying TLS data, and TLS records handed to SCTP MUST NOT have limited lifetimes.

Uni-directional streams cannot carry TLS data. They can be used without restriction for SCTP-based communication.
sections.eli5: A lane with a private tunnel should only carry tunnel traffic, and the packets must stay in order and never be thrown away.

sections.title: Handshake Patterns
sections.content:
The RFC walks through an association with two bi-directional streams, 0 and 1.

  • Full handshakes: the client sends a ClientHello on both streams right after the association is set up. Each stream can start carrying data when its own handshake finishes, independent of the other.
  • Abbreviated handshake: a full handshake runs on stream 0 and the server provides a session identifier. The client then resumes the session on stream 1 with an abbreviated handshake, and data can flow on stream 0 meanwhile.
  • Delayed abbreviated handshake: as above, but the second handshake waits until the user wants to send on stream 1, so resources are not spent at start-up for streams not yet used.
  • No full handshakes: both streams use abbreviated handshakes, which needs a valid session identifier from connections of another association.

Abbreviated handshakes can considerably cut computation when that is the limiting resource. But a full handshake must complete before one can resume, so in networks with long round-trip times it may be better to run several full handshakes in parallel. Both are allowed.
sections.eli5: You can do the full security check in every lane, or do it once and show your stamp in the others, or wait until you actually need a lane.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Running TLS over SCTP raises no new security issues beyond those in RFC 2246 and RFC 2960.

TLS endpoints can be authenticated by IP addresses in certificates. Unlike TCP, an SCTP endpoint can use multiple addresses, so TLS records may arrive from a different address than the one authenticated. That is fine as long as no security decision is based on that address. The general rule is that all decisions should rest on the peer's authenticated identity, not its transport layer identity.
sections.eli5: Trust who someone proves they are, not which door they walked through.
